get.summary: Owner only: accounts with role and sign-in source (no password data).

post.summary: Owner only: add an admin or guest account with a password.

delete.summary: Owner only: remove an account (not the owner); its sessions end.

get.summary: Sources that need a person (verification, sign-in): open items with the next automatic retry.

post.summary: Check an assistance item again now (in the background).
Sign in with name and password (login page). Failed attempts slow down and are logged.
Sign out. Ends every session of the account, on all devices.

get.summary: Who is calling: name, role and how they signed in.

post.summary: Change your own password; other sessions of the account end.
First boot: create the owner account (the first admin) and sign in. Refused once an owner exists.

get.summary: Sign-in method, whether the owner account still has to be created, and who is signed in.
The running values the UI needs to describe this instance.

The Connections menu: every connection type with its fields, the saved connections (secret values as {set} markers), the read-only ones derived from Settings, the last test of each, and the revision to send with a change.

post.summary: Add a connection: {revision, type, label?, enabled?, values}. Values are checked by field kind (URL, whole number, on/off, required); a type that allows one connection refuses a second, and a Suwayomi connection is refused (409) while MAIN_SUWAYOMI_URL is set in Settings. The answer's notice says what happens next (solver: the source host restarts; Suwayomi: the change feed reconnects; the first saved connection: how to roll back to 0.4.x).

Test values that are not saved yet: {type, values, id?}. With id, the values are applied onto that connection first, so a kept secret is tested with its saved value, unless an address now points at another server (then the secret must be sent again). Nothing is saved.

delete.summary: Delete a saved connection (?revision= names the revision it is based on). Connections from Settings are cleared on the Settings page.

put.summary: Change a saved connection: {revision, label?, enabled?, values?}. Fields left out keep their value; a secret sent as {set:true} or empty text is kept unless an address now points at another server (then it must be entered again); null clears a field. The answer's notice says what happens next.

get.summary: The stored one-time import plan of the main Suwayomi (Suwayomi connections only): status (awaiting-matching), saved_at, server_url and counts (total, sources, per source); plan is null before the first import.

post.summary: One-time import of the main Suwayomi library (Suwayomi connections only): {force?}. Queues a task that reads the library (read-only) and stores the plan; catalogue entries are created when matching arrives (conversion phase 8). With a plan stored, the task does nothing unless force is true. Answers 202 with the task id.

Test a saved connection (or one from Settings) without changing anything on the remote side, within 15 seconds: ok, a short message and details such as the version. The result is kept as the connection's last test.

get.summary: The newest 50 decisions of the decision log (merges, splits, separates, manual matches and groups, titles, reviews, resets) with their actor.

post.summary: Filter the decision log: body {kind (also matches dotted sub-kinds), entry_id, actor_kind, actor_name, record "source_id:source_manga_id", before (next_before of the previous page), limit (1-500)}.

get.summary: One decision with its before/after state.
PERF-9: all logs and diagnostics in one download, with secrets and private data removed.
Timing samples per work phase (no URLs, titles or keys).
Duplicate review badges for entries (?ids=1,2,...; at most 500) from the completed snapshot, never rescoring; pending while a refresh runs.

post.summary: Duplicate review badges for the entries in {"ids": [...]} (at most 500) from the completed snapshot, never rescoring.

get.summary: The duplicate review snapshot: groups of entries that may be one work, each pair with title/merge scores and whether the automatic gate would merge it; pending/stale while a refresh job runs, plus the automatic matching status.

post.summary: Run automatic duplicate matching now as a job: merge only pairs whose every original member passes the automatic gate (non-transitive); reviewed and separated pairs are never merged.

get.summary: Recorded automatic merges, newest first (offset, limit, q); older merges that kept only a reason are listed as legacy.
One recorded merge: both entries as they were before it, its evidence, and the entry it lives on now.

post.summary: Review a duplicate pair (left_entry_id, right_entry_id, decision): duplicate merges them and keeps the records together as a manual group, not_duplicate keeps them apart permanently, clear forgets the decision.
Check which API features the source or main engine answers (target: source or main) and save the report.

delete.summary: Delete an entry and suppress its source records so a refresh does not bring it back (owner or admin). Refused for main-library subscriptions unless the body says {force: true}.

post.summary: Add a manual alternative title: {title, language?}. The whole title is kept (never split) and becomes matching evidence for this entry. Returns the entry.

Bind the exact source record the user chose to the entry: body {source_id, source_manga_id, mode replace|add, candidate, defer_hydration}. With defer_hydration and the search card the choice commits at once and details load as a job.

get.summary: Search the catalogue by the entry's own names (main title, alternative and source titles, romanised forms): other entries with an exact shared title, plus the names used.

post.summary: Manual search: {query, source_id?, page?, all_names?}. With source_id, search that source live with the typed query and (all_names, default true) the entry's names; results are ranked by the matching scorer against the entry and show their current owner. Without source_id, search the catalogue.

delete.summary: Remove the manual main title and manual alternate titles of an entry (owner or admin); its main title returns to the most-used title of its records.
Detach every record of one source from the entry (their manual bindings are forgotten).

post.summary: Set the entry's main title: {title}. A manual main title is kept for this exact entry until it is removed or an explicit reset; it is recorded in the decision log. Returns the entry.

Redo an entry's automation as a job: keep the best-supported native record and manual/locked records, split every other automatic attachment back out, drop generated identities and titles, then search and refresh again.
Keep a source record as its own entry and remember it (body {source_id, source_manga_id, candidate}); the two entries are marked as different works.

delete.summary: Forget a separate-entry decision, so matching may attach the record to this entry again.

post.summary: Split every automatic source attachment off an entry (each to its own entry) and keep them apart (owner or admin); manual, imported, split and locked records stay.
Split the chosen source records off an entry into one new entry; the split is remembered as a manual decision so automation never re-joins them.

delete.summary: Remove an additional source record from an entry.

post.summary: Use an additional record as the primary record of its source; the old primary stays as an additional record.

get.summary: Recent errors grouped by cause with counts, newest first (resolved ones included).

post.summary: Remove resolved errors (or all errors with resolved_only=false).

get.summary: Status page: version, databases, catalogue counts, active errors and dependency checks.
Job queue: workers, running and queued jobs with ETA, and per-type run limit, average time, failures and freezes.
Keys page: the automatic admin token, the permanent admin key, reader keys (one per device) and script keys.

post.summary: Create a key (kind admin, reader or script; scripts are admin or guest). The secret is shown only in this answer.
Owner only: replace the automatic admin token; the old one stops working at once.

delete.summary: Revoke a key at once (a lost phone is cut off without touching other devices).

post.summary: Auto-merge duplicates across the catalogue as a job: recovers pending chapter work, then merges only pairs proven across every original member.

get.summary: Exactly which duplicate pairs the automatic gate would merge now (evidence only; the merge re-checks every pair).

post.summary: Full reset as an exclusive job (body {confirm: true}): clears the catalogue and every decision, keeps configuration and main-library subscriptions.

get.summary: Preview of resetting every saved manual decision (matches, groups, titles, separate rules, reviews, rejected chapters and imports, deleted-record suppression): counts per kind and the preview_token the confirmation must send back.

post.summary: Forget every saved manual decision (matches, groups, titles, separate rules, reviews, rejected chapters and imports, deleted-record suppression) after the preview was confirmed: body {confirm: true, preview_token}. Refused (409) when the decisions changed since the preview.
Invalidate every cached cover; source thumbnails are fetched again when shown.

Database reset as an exclusive job (body {confirm: true}): clears entries, automatic matches and titles, merge/split history and caches; keeps subscriptions, manual matches and groups (restored), deleted-record suppression and mixed-entry reviews; re-attaches different-works reviews, separate rules, manual titles, scopes and aliases to the restored works and drops (and counts) those whose work is not back.

get.summary: Preview of resetting the manual groups (matches stay attached and bound): counts per kind and the preview_token the confirmation must send back.

post.summary: Forget the manual groups (matches stay attached and bound) after the preview was confirmed: body {confirm: true, preview_token}. Refused (409) when the decisions changed since the preview.

get.summary: Preview of resetting the manual matches and groups (records stay attached as automatic ones): counts per kind and the preview_token the confirmation must send back.

post.summary: Forget the manual matches and groups (records stay attached as automatic ones) after the preview was confirmed: body {confirm: true, preview_token}. Refused (409) when the decisions changed since the preview.

get.summary: Merged entries whose source records can be split apart again, with every record and its match type.
Every saved user decision by kind: manual matches and groups, manual titles with their frozen record scope, separate-entry rules, rejected chapters and different-work reviews.
Persistent manual groups (two or more chosen records kept on one entry) and the individual manual matches.

post.summary: Catalogue records that could join a manual group: body {q, limit (1-100, default 60)}; best title match first.
Add an attached source record to a manual group: its entry is merged into the group's entry and the record is bound there.

delete.summary: Take a record out of its manual group; it stays attached but later rebuilds no longer keep it in the group.

get.summary: Matching rules per source and source group (internal / external matching), with their revision, the sources and groups they can name, and the matching profiles.

put.summary: Save the matching rule of one source or group and direction: {revision, rule: {enabled, checks} | null (inherit), reason?}. Title checks stay at 94% or more; identity and edition safeguards always apply.

get.summary: Matching profiles: ready-made presets (fixed), saved simple and advanced profiles with their effective scorer options, the preset revision and the default source ranking (official publisher sources, then health, then quality).

post.summary: Save a new matching profile: {revision, name, description?, rule} (0.4.5 rule {enabled, checks}) or {revision, name, description?, kind: simple|advanced, settings}. The title floor never goes below 94%.

delete.summary: Delete a saved matching profile: body {revision}. Ready-made profiles cannot be deleted.

put.summary: Change a saved matching profile (same body as create). Ready-made profiles are copied with Save as new instead.

get.summary: Entries whose source records may be different works (different formats, color editions, titles with unrelated detailed summaries), from the saved findings of the last mixed-entry check, with counts and the check's progress. Optional query: state, q, offset, limit.

post.summary: Start (or resume) the mixed-entry check as a job: the whole catalogue in bounded keyset batches, resumable after a restart. Body: restart (start over), auto_split (also split high-confidence automatic color/media mixtures), batch_size.

get.summary: One entry's source records with the pairwise evidence, its color/media edition profile (with every signal: title marker, page analysis, tags, source type, description) and the automatic split proposals.

post.summary: Keep this exact combination of source records together (decision keep) or forget that review (clear). The fingerprint must match the current evidence; nothing else changes.
Save the previewed policy when rules and evidence are unchanged; nothing is merged or split now. Logged with the signed-in actor.

get.summary: Sources, custom groups, saved matching rules (with revision) and presets for the policy simulator.

post.summary: Run the real matcher with the current and a draft policy: chosen pairs or a catalogue page at once, or the whole catalogue as a task (scan); lists works that would merge or split.

get.summary: Recent matching decisions with who made them (merges, splits, separate works, manual matches, title choices), reviewed batches and their undo state.

post.summary: Apply a previewed review batch when its revision still matches; logged as one decision with the signed-in actor.

get.summary: The audit trail of one work: its decisions with actors, its current source records and title.

post.summary: Check 1 to 100 review items (pairs to keep separate, or actions: separate, merge, split, manual.match, title) and return their effects and a revision.
Undo a reviewed batch while every work and decision it changed is still as the batch left it.

get.summary: Security log: sign-ins, failed sign-ins, slow-downs, key, token and account events, newest first; filter with ?kind=.
Effective settings grouped as on the Settings page; secret values are hidden.

put.summary: Save changed settings to config.json. Null resets a setting to its default; an empty secret removes it.

get.summary: What this start converted from autosourcarr.env to config.json.
The settings schema: name, type, default, description, secret, Compose variable and wizard step.
What the last update changed in your settings, until dismissed.

post.summary: Hide the update notice.

get.summary: Setup wizard fields with the current values; secrets show only whether one is saved.

post.summary: Save the wizard's changes to config.json in one step; a repeated request id returns the first result.
Check draft reader addresses and key without saving them.
Restart the integrated image to apply saved settings.

get.summary: Source browser identity (user-agent preset and value), presets, the identity the engine uses now and the WebView state.

post.summary: Remove the engine's cookies and browser data (sign-ins and Cloudflare clearances). Installed extensions stay.
Apply the saved repositories and load every installed extension again (new headers, changed settings). Installed extensions and sign-ins stay.

put.summary: Save the source browser identity and apply it to the running engine (sources rebuild their headers).

get.summary: Source engine status: mode, state, readiness, restarts, last error and the Cloudflare handlers (WebView, FlareSolverr).

post.summary: Report the Cloudflare handlers now. The source host solves challenges when a source meets one; queued is true when a handler is ready.

get.summary: Installed and available extensions from the configured repositories (?refresh=true reloads the repositories).

post.summary: Update every installed extension that has a newer version.

Check a source APK (archive structure, manifest and entry point, no native code) and list its permissions, web addresses and warnings; nothing is installed. The file waits 10 minutes for POST /source-extensions/upload/confirm with its sha256.
Install a source APK checked by POST /source-extensions/upload (body: sha256) within 10 minutes of its check.
Install, update or uninstall an extension; the source list refreshes in the background.
Create a source group (members share one priority; the member with the most chapters serves).

delete.summary: Delete a source group; its members become ungrouped.

put.summary: Rename a source group or change its priority.

get.summary: Source repair status: worker configuration, the daily check switch and the last repair promotion and which repair kinds can run.
Last automatic repair pass and the attempts per package.

post.summary: Start an automatic repair pass of moved sources now (REP-6).

get.summary: Where repairs run: always inside this instance (no external worker); which repair kinds are available.

put.summary: Retired: external repair worker connections were removed (410).

get.summary: In-app repair state: domain repair availability, whether a repair is running, AI provider (not configured until Connections) and the runner check.

post.summary: Repair control actions: check (or prepare) runs the repair runner self-check; account actions answer 409 until an AI provider is configured.

get.summary: Retired: the repair host-policy bundle was removed with the external worker (410).
Installed source extensions with their package, version, repository and source identities.

post.summary: Start a domain-move repair of an installed source (body: pkg_name, optional new_host, old_host, query, https) as a job; answers the job's task id.

get.summary: A repair job: its task (state, progress, message) and the matching repair report (migration, structure and content checks, rollback).

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running repair job; a repair that already changed the source rolls back itself.

get.summary: Download the repaired jar a domain repair installed (kept copy, or the installed jar when its digest still matches); 404 otherwise.

post.summary: Discard a repair: when it installed a repaired jar, the jar kept before it is installed again (a rollback job); otherwise nothing changes.
Feedback on the current installed repair (action fixed, retry or revert; installed_sha256 must match). Kept in feedback.jsonl (bounded); revert queues a rollback.

get.summary: Download the working jar that was kept before the repair (a JAR is a ZIP).

post.summary: Domain repairs install themselves: for a repaired job this answers 200 with its report and changes nothing; otherwise 409.
Keep the original APK of an installed source as repair evidence (headers confirm the original and its version).

get.summary: The repair AI provider; answers state not-configured until AI providers arrive with Connections.

post.summary: Test the repair AI provider (409 while none is configured).

get.summary: Raw-code state of an installed source (needs-input, acquiring, available, reconstructing); adopts retained repair code that matches the installed binary.
Download the retained source code of an installed source as a portable ZIP.

post.summary: Look up the source's repository in the configured indexes (body: revision); runs in the background.
Fetch the source code from its original public repository (body: revision, origin {repository, module, revision, ecosystem}).
Upload the source project ZIP of an installed source (headers X-Raw-Revision, X-Source-Version, optional X-Source-Module; at most 32 MiB). Kept private.
Ask for new source code input again (body: revision).
The code is unavailable: rebuild the source from its installed binary (body: revision, optional job_id). Needs an AI provider; 409 until Connections.
Install the working jar kept before the last repair of a package again, as a job (body pkg_name; without a body, the package of the last installed repair record).
Retired: Compose/SSH repair worker setup was removed (410).

put.summary: Turn automatic repair of moved sources on or off (domain repairs need no worker).

get.summary: Details of one title as its source reports them (refreshed from the source).
Orphaned sources under two headers, Installed and Not installed, each with its own orphan group (SRC-3); items lists them all, with discovery and installation state.

post.summary: Collect removed sources from sampled original Keiyoushi history (two years) in the background; at most once a minute.
Install the original archived package of a removed source (digest and package identity checked; never replaces an installed source).
Mark an installed source as orphaned (only when it is missing from the configured repositories).
Repair an installed orphan by moving it to its new web address (forwards to /api/v1/source-repairs/{pkgName}/domain).
Return an installed orphan to the Installed list.

get.summary: The last repair or rollback report of a package (state repaired, refused, failed, rolled_back or rollback_failed, with the migration, structure and content checks).

post.summary: Repair an installed source whose website moved: keep its jar, rewrite the old host in its compiled strings (new_host, or the observed redirect), check the structure, install, check content, and roll back when the check fails. Runs as a job.
Install the last kept working jar of a package again (as a job).

get.summary: Available sources with enabled, priority, group and language choices, and the source groups.

post.summary: Read the installed sources from the engine and store them (new sources get the default choices; empty engine lists keep existing ones).

put.summary: Change a source's choices: enabled, priority, group, official, matching rules.

get.summary: The extension's own settings for this source (as in Mihon), with current values.

put.summary: Change one extension setting of this source.

get.summary: Catalogue, chapter, source, cache and storage counts; refreshed at most every 15 seconds.
Where the databases are and how large they are.

post.summary: Copy, check and switch both databases to another mounted folder (SET-5); the old files are kept.

get.summary: Main Suwayomi library entries from the AutoSourcarr source, mapped to catalogue entries: entry_ids, items, stats_by_entry (chapter and downloaded counts), ok and error.
The tag synonym map: built-in synonyms, your synonyms and the effective list (namespace, from, to, origin), with its revision.

put.summary: Replace your tag synonyms (body: synonyms [{namespace, from, to}], optional revision from the last read). Mapping a built-in synonym to itself switches it off. Creator, character, parody and language names cannot be synonyms.

get.summary: Ongoing, completed and failed tasks with progress, ETA and finish time; job type, priority and queue position for queued work; repair jobs are listed as kind source-repair with package and repair state.

post.summary: Remove completed and failed tasks from the list; running and queued work stays.
Cancel a queued or running task. Work already done stays; the task is listed as failed with "Cancelled by user".
Replay an interrupted task only when replaying it cannot change data twice (read-only observations).
